title: The Ides of Slightly Different Opinions
skyStory: The Ides of March arrive with a first quarter moon in Gemini, exactly half lit and arguing with itself about which half is better. Mercury moderates the debate badly. The light side says go. The dark side says wait. Both are right, which is very annoying. Somewhere a pair of mittens is having the same argument.

reading: You will hear two good opinions today that completely contradict each other, and you will want to pick a side immediately. The Tiger likes to pounce. But the half-lit moon suggests a different move: wait until tomorrow morning. The right answer is shy and arrives late.

This is a patience day disguised as a decision day. The [[Two of Swords]] sits blindfolded in your path, balancing both choices without dropping either. You do not have to choose yet. Put both options in an imaginary jar and give the jar a shake before bed. Look at it again over breakfast. The answer will float to the top by itself, like a cork.
joel.mission: Postpone one non-urgent decision until tomorrow morning and write the two options on separate pieces of paper.
joel.omen: Two birds arguing on a branch. It means both sides of your question have merit, so do not rush.

reading: Patience is your native language, so today is a good one for you. While everyone else flaps around making Ides of March jokes, you will move steadily through the day like the tide, getting exactly where you are going without needing anyone to notice.

Around 3 pm, someone will ask your opinion on something with two sides. Give them a third option they had not considered. The Wood Rat has a gift for finding the hidden door in a room with two obvious exits. They will look at you like you just pulled a coin from their ear. Smile serenely. Say nothing more.
nancy.mission: When someone offers you two choices today, propose a third option, even if it is silly, just to see what happens.
nancy.omen: A path that forks in the snow or mud. It means there is a third way, and you will see it first.
nancy.stoneWhy: layers show more than two sides

together.text: Gemini debate night. Pick a deeply silly topic, like whether pancakes are just flat cake, and argue opposite sides for five texts each. Then switch sides and argue the other way. Nobody wins. Everybody laughs. Mercury takes notes for future reference.

game.intro: Beware the Ides of slightly different opinions. Disagree loudly, love each other anyway.
